cases.purpose: LinkedIn post generation sends a personal achievement; Gemini's free tier (no paid tier attested in default config) may use content to improve products, so it must be ineligible.
A whole CV must not go to a user-supplied Gemini key whose tier Wasl cannot verify (may be free tier).
Groq does not retain inputs by default (≤30-day abuse logging only), which meets the limited-retention floor for personal data.
OpenRouter requests are forced to zero-data-retention endpoints, so repository analysis is allowed even with a user key.
CV tailoring rewrites personal CV content and must not be routed to the Gemini free tier.
Extracting requirements from a public job ad contains no personal data, so the Gemini free tier is acceptable.
Batch extraction from many public job ads is public data and may use any provider, including an unknown-tier personal Gemini key.
The learning roadmap is built from the user's own verified/unverified/missing skill profile (personal), so an unknown-tier Gemini key is not allowed.
Deriving job-search titles from the Master CV processes personal data and must not use the Gemini free tier.
Groq's no-retention-by-default policy applies to user keys too, so a CV update via the user's Groq key meets the floor.
